library(tidyverse)

# Problem 1

### Create a birthday function
Write a function that, for a fixed group size, randomly draws “birthdays” for each person
```{r}
birthday_check = function(n) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)

  n_distinct(birthdays) < n
}
```

### Test the function
duplicate birthdays in the group; and returns TRUE or FALSE based on the result.
```{r}
set.seed(1)
birthday_check(7)
birthday_check(77)
birthday_check(245)
```

### Run the simulations
Next, run this function 10000 times for each group size between 2 and 50.
```{r}
set.seed(1)

birthday_results = 
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |> 
  mutate(shared_birthday = map_lgl(group_size, birthday_check))
```


### Calculate the probabilities
compute the probability that at least two people in the group will share a birthday by averaging across the 10000 simulation runs.
```{r}
birthday_summary = 
  birthday_results |> 
  group_by(group_size) |> 
  summarize(probability = mean(shared_birthday))
birthday_summary
```

### Plot the results
Make a plot showing the probability as a function of group size, and comment on your results.
```{r}
birthday_summary |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_point() + 
  labs(
    title = "Probability of sharing a birthday by group size",
    x = "Group size",
    y = "Probability of at least one shared birthday"
  )
```

TThe chance of a shared birthday increases pretty quickly as the group gets bigger. It first passes 50% at a group size of `r birthday_summary |> filter(probability > 0.5) |> pull(group_size) |> min()`. By the time there are 50 people, the probability reaches `r round(birthday_summary |> filter(group_size == 50) |> pull(probability), 2)`. This is surprising because even a small group can have many possible pairs of people, making a shared birthday more likely.

## Problem 3

### Create a simulation function
First, I created a function to simulates a dataset
```{r}
sim_t_test = function(mu, n = 30, sigma = 5) {
  sim_data = tibble(
    x = rnorm(n, mean = mu, sd = sigma)
  )
  t.test(pull(sim_data, x), mu = 0) |> 
    broom::tidy() |> 
    select(estimate, p.value)
}
```

### Test the function
```{r}
sim_t_test(mu = 0)
sim_t_test(mu = 4)
```
### Run the simulations
Generate 5000 datasets from the model
```{r}
sim_results_df = 
  expand_grid(
    mu = 0:6,
    iter = 1:5000
  ) |> 
  mutate(estimate_df = map(mu, sim_t_test)) |> 
  unnest(estimate_df)
```

### Calculate power
test of 𝐻:𝜇=0 using 𝛼=0.05
```{r}
power_df = 
  sim_results_df |> 
  group_by(mu) |> 
  summarize(power = mean(p.value < 0.05))
power_df 
```

### Plot power
```{r}
power_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = mu, y = power)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_point() + 
  labs(
    title = "Power of a one-sample t-test by true mean",
    x = "True value of μ",
    y = "Proportion of times the null was rejected"
  )
```
